correctness.rationale: The set of eligible endpoints is a nonempty proper coordinate box under CRT, proving the exact least period; all r-fold consecutive blocks are one length-(k+r-1) block, giving the product A_{k,r}; two boundary exclusions yield R_{k,r}. For two distinct primes the CRT construction makes both adjacent endpoints fail while the central r survive; a single prime gives one cyclic run. The known second Ramanujan prime R_2=11 and the four small k cases give exactly k=3,5 as intermediate-support exceptions. The complete all-parameter proof is explicit in RESULT.md. An independent finite enumeration of all original factors for 18 k and additional product checks for k<2000 corroborate but do not replace the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader CRT correlation theorem for von Neumann regular residues was compared by its actual hypotheses. For squarefree M_k every residue is regular, unlike the k-forbidden-residue window; its run law cannot specialize to this indicator. Ordinary CRT counting supplies the one-point tool, but previously inspected results do not assert or cover the strict support dichotomy for these prime-window blocks.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper proves a lower bound for the first admissible endpoint, and the earlier density note provides the one-point CRT proportion. Neither inspected claim states the exact least period, full maximal-run counts, or the complete all-k run-support exception list. Previously published generic regular-residue run formulas concern a different local property: regularity modulo a squarefree modulus is automatic, whereas the present forbidden k-residue windows are not. Generic CRT and second-difference techniques are acknowledged as antecedents, not claimed as new. Risk remains of an implicit derivation in the inaccessible full 2025 note.

value.rationale: The theorem is a natural complete finite-period clustering invariant of the recently studied Erdős prime-window avoidance process, a genuine refinement of the previously known one-point density. It gives exact sharp period, all run multiplicities, next-prime-gap cutoff, and the surprising complete support classification with only k=3,5 as exceptions. This distinguishes local clustering from mean density and the open first-hit question; no unsupported general first-hit consequence is claimed. The result is a complete uniform classification, not an arbitrary finite cutoff.
